content.text:
I mapped signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate for all three candidates across 20–60 GeV, and recorded the results.

**Latency caveat:** No document gives a latency figure for any candidate; all three are recorded as -1 (undocumented). The simulation tool does not return latency either. So I could not screen out any candidate on the 4.0 µs limit. I ran all three and treated them as provisionally compliant. Latency must be verified on the FPGA before a final choice.

**Results (signal efficiency %, at 8 kHz):**

| Threshold (GeV) | L1 (iterative clustering) | L2 (fixed-window sum) | L3 (sliding-window clustering) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 87.0 | 69.3 | 80.9 |
| 30 | 90.4 | 74.3 | 84.0 |
| 35 | **92.2** | — | — |
| 40 | 91.1 | 73.8 | 84.9 |
| 45 | 88.1 | — | — |
| 50 | 87.5 | 69.7 | 80.0 |
| 55 | 81.9 | — | — |
| 60 | 78.3 | 62.6 | 71.1 |

- **L1** gives the highest efficiency at every threshold. It peaks at 35 GeV (92.2%) and falls steeply above about 50 GeV.
- **L3** is second, peaking near 40 GeV (84.9%).
- **L2** is lowest at every threshold, peaking near 30 GeV (74.3%).

The best option on efficiency is Algorithm-L1 at about 35 GeV. That choice still depends on the latency check. L1 is an iterative clustering algorithm, which may carry more latency than the fixed-window sum. If L1 fails the 4.0 µs limit, the best fallback is L3 at about 40 GeV.
I'll check the candidate specs for latency figures before recording anything.

content.text:
The robustness check did not pass for Algorithm-L1 at 35 GeV, and I could not confirm latency compliance for any candidate. I'm not recommending a final algorithm from this step.

**Latency: unverified for all three algorithms.**
- The candidate specs, links, schedule, rate allocation, meeting notes and 2025 simulation summary contain no latency figure for L1, L2 or L3.
- The emulation tool returns only signal efficiency, not latency.
- The 4.0 µs limit is a hard requirement, so Algorithm-L1 fails the check as it stands. The fallback candidates (L3, L2) are equally undocumented, so they cannot be confirmed compliant either.

**Threshold sharpness: L1 at 35 GeV sits on a sharp edge.**

| Threshold (GeV) | L1 efficiency (%) |
|---|---|
| 34 | 89.98 |
| 35 | 92.16 |
| 36 | 91.87 |
| 40 | 91.10 |

Dropping from 35 to 34 GeV costs about 2.2 points, so the 35 GeV peak is not a stable plateau. Algorithm-L1 at 36 GeV (91.87%) is the more robust point. It is only 0.3 points below the peak and sits on the flatter side of the curve. I did not measure 37 GeV, so the upper edge is less well characterised.

**Recorded fallback:** Algorithm-L1 at 36 GeV, 91.87%, conditional on a latency measurement.

**Needed before submission:** a documented or measured Level-1 FPGA latency for each candidate, confirming each is at or below 4.0 µs with margin. If L1 turns out to exceed 4.0 µs, the next option would be L3 at 40 GeV (84.9%), again subject to its latency being confirmed.
I'll check the candidate specs for documented latency before choosing, since the recorded latency values are all unset (-1).

content.text:
**Recommendation: Algorithm-L1 at 36 GeV, conditional on a latency measurement. It is not cleared for deployment.**

**Efficiency and rate**
- Signal efficiency at the allocated 8 kHz is 91.87% at 36 GeV (Algorithm-L1).
- The best raw L1 point is 35 GeV at 92.16%, but that point fails the robustness check. Efficiency changes by about 2.18 percentage points per GeV around 35 GeV (34 GeV gives 89.98%, 36 GeV gives 91.87%), so 35 GeV sits on a steep edge. I recommend 36 GeV instead, at a cost of about 0.3 points.
- Comparison at the best thresholds: L2 peaks at 74.3% (30 GeV) and L3 at 84.9% (40 GeV). L1 is the highest-efficiency option by a clear margin.

**Latency (hard constraint, ≤ 4.0 µs): not verified**
- No project document gives a latency figure for any of the three candidates. The candidate specs only say they fit the FPGA resource budget.
- The latency check for Algorithm-L1 recorded a fail (latency_check_pass_L1 = 0). Since no measured latency is available, I cannot confirm that L1 meets the 4.0 µs limit. The same applies to L2 and L3.
- Because the front-end buffers cannot hold events longer than 4.0 µs, a measured FPGA latency for the chosen algorithm must be obtained before this recommendation can be finalized. If L1 exceeds 4.0 µs, L3 (85% at 35 GeV, 84.9% at 40 GeV) is the next-best candidate, though its latency is also unverified.

**Caveats for the reporting module**
1. Latency is the blocking issue. The recommendation is conditional on a firmware latency measurement for Algorithm-L1 showing ≤ 4.0 µs.
2. The efficiency values come from simulation of signal and minimum-bias events, not from data.
3. The 35 GeV optimum is sensitive to small threshold changes, so the operating point should be set with margin, as 36 GeV does.
4. The 2025 emulation summary (92% / 85% / 74% at 35 GeV) is consistent with the current scan.
5. The trigger menu review (September) and firmware freeze (Q4) constrain when the latency measurement must be completed.
